fix_assessment.rationale: The reported sequencing suggests Workspaces may arrange the transient splash window before the main window appears; the discussion has no code-level proof, and the Word /q workaround is application-specific.

proposed_fixes.title: Arrange the main application window after its splash screen closes
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: Workspaces may apply saved placement to a transient splash screen and fail to reapply it to the application's main window after the splash closes. This has not been verified on BankTree or a current build.
plan: Reproduce with the original BankTree application and capture which HWND Workspaces detects during the splash and after the main window appears.
Compare launch behavior with the splash enabled and, where supported, disabled; also test the documented Word /q argument only for Word.

If Workspaces targets a transient splash window, wait for the main window or reapply the saved geometry after the splash closes, while preserving applications that intentionally use separate splash windows.
Add regression coverage using an app with a separate splash and main window; do not treat Word's /q workaround as a general fix.
verification: Launching the BankTree workspace places its main window at the saved position and size after the splash closes.
The splash window is not incorrectly resized or positioned as the final application window.
Verify a second application with a distinct splash window and a normal application with no splash are unaffected.

confidence.rationale: The described ordering and named application support a testable transient-window hypothesis, but current behavior and the actual window identities have not been observed.

issue_context.summary: Workspaces reportedly resizes and moves a startup splash screen, then fails to arrange the main application window correctly.
known_information: The issue reports PowerToys 0.84.1, installed from GitHub, and Workspaces not running as administrator.
The original author named BankTree as the most affected application after a maintainer asked for an example.
A second commenter named Microsoft Word; /q was suggested as an application-specific splash suppression argument.
That commenter later described a separate FancyZones snapping problem and said Word placement could be corrected with macros.
inferences: The splash and main window may have different handles/lifetimes, which could explain placement being applied to the wrong window.
The Word argument workaround does not establish a general Workspaces fix or resolve the BankTree report.
